name: Book Edge Sweep
rule: Generate a candidate when a fresh YES or NO ask is at or below 45¢ and the displayed spread is at least 2¢.
why: A return-seeking price dislocation hypothesis that uses only the current Kalshi book. It is not a claim that the dislocation is an arbitrage.
evidence: Kalshi market quote plus a fresh order-book snapshot

name: Last-Tick Momentum
rule: Generate a candidate only when the API provides both last and previous prices and the move is at least 3¢ in one direction; buy that direction at the live ask.
why: A simple momentum hypothesis whose input and date are observable. It can fail when the last trade is stale or liquidity is thin, so a fill is still book-dependent.
evidence: Kalshi last price, previous price, current quote and order book

name: Expiry Tail Sprint
rule: Flag contracts inside 48 hours of close when an executable side is at or below 15¢; no outcome is assumed and no fill is created without depth.
why: A deliberately aggressive expiry hypothesis for the return leaderboard. The result must be judged against the official settlement result or a verified exit book, not a guessed outcome.
evidence: Kalshi close time, status, quote and order book

name: Depth Imbalance
rule: Use the total displayed YES versus NO depth as a directional candidate only when both sides have fresh levels and imbalance exceeds 35%.
why: Tests whether visible depth predicts short-run price movement. It explicitly logs the book levels because displayed liquidity can disappear before a paper fill.
evidence: Kalshi order-book levels and retrieval timestamp

name: Market-Making Quote Plan
rule: Place a simulated two-sided quote inside a measured spread and wait for future verified market-data evidence before calling it filled.
why: Tests market-making economics, queue uncertainty and maker-fee differences. A REST snapshot cannot prove queue position or a maker fill, so this roster entry creates plans, not fake fills.
evidence: Kalshi order book, fee schedule and later trade/order-book update

name: Momentum Cross (Pine-style)
rule: Long when last price > slow SMA and fast SMA > slow SMA (daily 5/10, hourly 3/6); exit when last price < slow SMA at the verified bid; else hold to official settlement.
why: Classic trend-following on a verified tape. The committed result shows both failure modes: 1-tick range crosses that stop out against the spread, and the genuine breakout that paid.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (cross-chaser rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Cheap Dip Hunter
rule: Buy YES at the verified ask when ask <= 0.05 on a bar with volume; exit at the first verified bid >= 2x entry, else hold to settlement.
why: Return-seeking lottery tickets: pay pennies, need a double or a 100% payoff. The committed tape shows why it bleeds — one-sided books keep the YES bid at zero, so exits never verify and cheap tickets settle at zero.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (dip-hunter rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Release Spike Surfer
rule: Buy in the direction of a bar whose |last - previous last| >= 0.20 AND volume >= 3x the average of the prior 10 volume bars; exit at the first verified bid above entry, else hold to settlement.
why: Chases information releases when the verified tape shows both a jump and heavy official volume. The committed window contained exactly one qualifying spike (the NFL final-drive bar) and it paid; the CPI release spike failed the 3x volume gate, which is the documented trap-avoidance.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (spike-surfer rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Favorite Holder
rule: Buy YES at the verified ask when bar close >= 0.90 and bar volume >= 100,000 contracts; hold to official settlement.
why: Favorite-longshot-bias play: heavy favorites on event markets are often slightly under-priced. Only enters when the verified tape proves a liquid 90+ cent favorite — in the committed window that happened once (NFL 95 cents) and settled to $1.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (sure-thing rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Certainty Carry
rule: Buy NO at the verified NO ask (1 - YES bid) when NO ask is in [0.97, 0.99] (YES bid 0.01-0.03), the bar has volume, and official settlement is within 21 days; hold to settlement. NO asks below 0.97 are lottery tickets and are rejected.
why: Earns the residual on near-certain outcomes with a hard time horizon. The committed tape produced one qualifying bar (CPI, NO ask 0.99, 18.5 days to settlement) that settled to $1 for a small positive PnL; the NFL 32-cent NO ask is correctly rejected as not carry.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (yield-sniper rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: NWS Forecast Edge
rule: Compare a versioned National Weather Service forecast with a matching Kalshi weather contract only after location, measurement window and settlement rule are verified.
why: Weather is useful only if the forecast variable exactly matches the contract. NWS is a primary source; the user's SFWeather project is a research link, not a price oracle.
evidence: NWS API response + Kalshi contract terms + live Kalshi book

name: SEC Form 4 Catalyst
rule: Use a filed SEC Form 4 transaction only after accession, filing time, issuer and transaction code are captured; it must map to a Kalshi event before a signal is possible.
why: The SEC filing is primary evidence for the filing, not evidence of a Kalshi outcome. This is a cross-domain hypothesis and stays blocked until a contract mapping exists.
evidence: SEC EDGAR filing + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: FDA Decision Catalyst
rule: Use a dated FDA action or official Drugs@FDA record only when the Kalshi event's issuer, drug and settlement date match exactly.
why: FDA records can verify a regulatory action but cannot be substituted for a market quote or settlement result. The user DrugAnalysis site remains a research index with manual primary-source review.
evidence: FDA official record + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: NFL Official Status
rule: Require an official NFL injury designation with timestamp and a contract whose terms can be joined to the affected game.
why: The user's NFL Injury Report documents official nfl.com values where published, but a report is not a price and ESPN fallback data is not official NFL confirmation.
evidence: NFL official report + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: NBA Report Gate
rule: Do not trade from a third-party injury post; require a dated official NBA report and a verified matching contract.
why: The MasterSite audit explicitly flags the absence of a machine-readable official NBA live injury feed. This strategy is visible for research but cannot generate a verified trade here.
evidence: Official NBA report if available + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: NCAA Score Trigger
rule: Join a live or final score from an official NCAA scoreboard to an exact Kalshi event and record the score timestamp before evaluating a signal.
why: The scoreboard can verify a game state, but only Kalshi's book and terms can verify an executable contract trade.
evidence: NCAA scoreboard + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: NFL Score Trigger
rule: Use an official NFL score/play state only after matching team names, game date and contract settlement rule.
why: The user's scoreboard project is useful for research discovery, but it is not itself the exchange or settlement authority.
evidence: NFL official scoreboard or game data + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: MLB Game-State Trigger
rule: Use official MLB game-state data only after mapping the exact game and the contract's settlement condition.
why: MLB Gameday can verify the game state. It cannot establish the price, fill or settlement of a Kalshi contract.
evidence: MLB Stats/Gameday + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book

name: Cross-Sport Model
rule: Treat SportsPred output as a hypothesis only; re-score it using an identified official game source and compare against a live Kalshi quote.
why: The user's SportsPred project is not an official data authority. This gate prevents a model output or social pick from entering the verified ledger as fact.
evidence: Official sport source + model version + Kalshi terms and book

name: Gold Macro Join
rule: When the Kalshi gold contract names a reference and window that matches a stored official publication timestamp, trade only against that contract's verified book; otherwise no signal.
why: A jewelry listing or third-party gold quote is not a settlement oracle. The user's GOLD directory is a buyer's reference and is not used as a market price.
evidence: Official benchmark/commodity source + Kalshi terms + live Kalshi book. name: Pine Signal Replay
rule: Translate a Pine strategy into a fully specified rule, then replay only against timestamped Kalshi prices that existed at the decision time.
why: PinePilot's calculator is not a verified Kalshi tape. This strategy is eligible for future research once raw official candlesticks or trades are archived.
evidence: Kalshi historical endpoint + versioned rule + no look-ahead

name: The Leap Research Map
rule: Use The Leap's official rules and instrument universe to form a hypothesis, never as a substitute for a Kalshi market or verified price.
why: The Leap is a separate paper-trading contest. Its results and rules are useful research context, but they do not prove a Kalshi strategy return.
evidence: TradingView/AMP Futures contest terms + Kalshi data if a contract mapping exists
